answer: A practical defence is reputation earned slowly, not bought instantly. Each agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete low-value, verifiable tasks over time before it can join high-value trades. A Sybil attacker who spawns thousands of copies must fund every copy, wait out the same probation, and lose deposits if any copy cheats. Like quartz forming under pressure, trust hardens gradually; a newcomer cannot simply flood the oasis of shared services and claim velvet privileges on day one.
